name: Hanging Oblique Knee Raise
cues: Hang from the bar with straight arms
Raise your knees toward one shoulder
Curl your pelvis up as the knees rise

qa.note: Wave 3b 2026-10-09: rated minor, owner review. needs work: At the top the left elbow bends to 34.8 deg while the right stays at 6.0 (frames 0-24 and 96-110). The bend is clearly visible in the hero frames t=0 and 0.125 and contradicts cue 1 'Hang from the bar with straight arms'. It is an IK artifact of the 7 cm root shift: the nearer grip leaves slack, and the elbow absorbs it. | minor: Elbow defect fixed. A new solve (hangPoseRolled in leg-raise.ts, oblique raise only) slides the body sideways under the bar and rolls it about the forward axis, solving root x/y/z plus roll by damped least squares so both shoulders stay at the straight-arm distance from their grips and the CoM stays under the bar's middle. Elbows are now 5.6-8.0 deg (left) and 6.0-6.1 deg (right) across the loop. They were 34.8/6.0. Each hand's world orientation is splined over the 13 knots so the wrists don't chatter (the first try failed the jerk gate at frame 85). The context solve dropped from about 15-40 s to about 2-4 s, so still.ts --live works now. New tests: both elbows under 10 deg on every frame, and the 'thorax square' check rewritten as joint-line yaw (femur over 40, humerus under 8 deg), because a world roll breaks the old DOF-sum identity. The shoulder line was already yawed about 7 deg at the top before my change (7.2 with the roll disabled), so that isn't a regression. What remains: the four-bar swing is large. At the top the shoulder midpoint sits about 0.19 m off centre with a 6 deg tilt, one arm runs clearly diagonal in the figure sheet, and the feet come within 69 mm of the frame upright. It reads as a pendulum swing, which the reviewer allowed, but it is a lot of swing. QA passes, bake is fresh.
